library(meraconstraints)

## IV inequalities

```{r}
ivdag <- graph_from_literal(Z -+ X, X -+ Y, U -+ X:Y) |> initialize_graph()
ivrels <- dag_get_linear_relations(ivdag)
dag_list_independences(ivdag)

hrepiv <- cf_relations_to_hrep(ivrels)
hrep_to_text(hrepiv$Hrep[[1]], ivrels$probform[[1]])
hrep_to_text(hrepiv$Hrep[[1]], ivrels$probform[[1]])[prob_simplex_extremes(ivrels, hrepiv$Hrep)[[1]]]
```

Rows 2, 3, 5 and 6 are the familiar IV inequalities. As you can see below, when we sample distributions unconstrained, only those 4 are ever violated. 

```{r}
ptable <- data.table(expand.grid(X = 0:1, Y = 0:1, Z = 0:1))

sprob <- function(k) {
  diff(sort(c(runif(k - 1), 0, 1)))
}

res <- matrix(NA, nrow = 2000, ncol = 14)
for(i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  # ptable$pv <- NA
  # ptable$pv[c(1:4)] <- sprob(4)
  # ptable$pv[c(5:8)] <- sprob(4)
  ptable$joint <- sprob(8)
  ptable[, pXZ := sum(joint), by = .(X, Z)]
  ptable[, pXY := sum(joint), by = .(X, Y)]
  ptable[, pZ := sum(joint), by = .(Z)]
  ptable[, pX := sum(joint), by = .(X)]
  ptable[, pv := (pXZ / pZ) * (pXY / pX)]
  
  res[i, ] <- hrep_test(hrepiv$Hrep[[1]], ptable$pv, which = TRUE)[, 1]
  
}
colMeans(res)
```

## Sequential IV example

```{r}
ivdag2 <- graph_from_literal(V1 -+ V2 -+ V3 -+ V4 -+ V5, U1 -+ V2:V3, U2 -+ V4:V5) |> initialize_graph()
dag_list_independences(ivdag2)

ivrels2 <- dag_get_linear_relations(ivdag2)
hrepiv2 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(ivrels2)

prob_simplex_extremes(ivrels2, hrepiv2$Hrep)

ptable1 <- expand.grid(V3 = 0:1, V2 = 0:1, V1 = 0:1)
ptable2 <- expand.grid(V4 = 0:1, V5 = 0:1, V3 = 0:1)

sprob <- function(k) {
  diff(sort(c(runif(k - 1), 0, 1)))
}

res <- matrix(NA, nrow = 2000, ncol = sum(sapply(hrepiv2$Hrep, nrow)))
for(i in 1:nrow(res)) {
  ptable1$pv <- ptable2$pv <- NA
  ptable1$pv[c(1:4)] <- sprob(4)
  ptable1$pv[c(5:8)] <- sprob(4)
  ptable2$pv[c(1:4)] <- sprob(4)
  ptable2$pv[c(5:8)] <- sprob(4)

  res[i, ] <- c(hrep_test(hrepiv2$Hrep[[1]], ptable1$pv, which = TRUE)[, 1], 
                hrep_test(hrepiv2$Hrep[[2]], ptable2$pv, which = TRUE)[, 1])
  
}
colMeans(res)

c(hrep_to_text(hrepiv2$Hrep[[1]], ivrels2$probform[[1]]), 
hrep_to_text(hrepiv2$Hrep[[2]], ivrels2$probform[[2]]))[which(colMeans(res) < 1)]
```

## Robin's example

```{r}
r1dag <- graph_from_literal(V1 -+ V2 -+ V3 -+ V4, V1 -+ V4, U2 -+ V2:V4) |> initialize_graph()
r2dag <- graph_from_literal(V1 -+ V2 -+ V3 -+ V4, V2 -+ V4, U2 -+ V2:V4) |> initialize_graph()

dag_list_independences(r1dag)
dag_list_independences(r2dag)

r1rels <- dag_get_linear_relations(r1dag)
r1hreps <- cf_relations_to_hrep(r1rels)

r2rels <- dag_get_linear_relations(r2dag)
r2hreps <- cf_relations_to_hrep(r2rels)

hrep_to_text(r1hreps$Hrep[[2]], r1rels$probform[[2]]) ## trivial
hrep_to_text(r2hreps$Hrep[[2]], r2rels$probform[[2]]) ## trivial
```


Let's see if we can distinguish these two models:
```{r}

hrep_to_text(r1hreps$Hrep[[1]], r1rels$probform[[1]])[prob_simplex_extremes(r1rels, r1hreps$Hrep)[[1]]]
hrep_to_text(r2hreps$Hrep[[1]], r2rels$probform[[1]])[prob_simplex_extremes(r2rels, r2hreps$Hrep)[[1]]]

res <- matrix(NA, nrow = 1000, ncol = nrow(r2hreps$Hrep[[1]]))
for(i in 1:nrow(res)) {

  probs <- dag_sample_distribution(r1dag, parmsamp = \(k) rnorm(k, sd = 5))
  probs1 <- merge(probs$V4, probs$V2, by = "V1")
  probs1$prob <- with(probs1, probs.x * probs.y)
  probs1 <- probs1[with(probs1, order(V3, V1, V4, V2)),]


  res[i,] <- hrep_test(r2hreps$Hrep[[1]], probs1$prob, which = TRUE)
             
}

hrep_to_text(r2hreps$Hrep[[1]], r2rels$probform[[1]])[colMeans(res) < 1]
```

These are 4 nontrivial inequality constraints that can tell us that a distribution sampled from model 1 does not come from model 2. The other direction does not work, if we sample from model 2, we cannot distinguish it from model 1. 


## Incomplete linear example

```{r}
duarg <- graph_from_literal(A -+ B -+ C -+ D, A -+ E -+ C, D -+ F, U1 -+ A:C:E, U2 -+ F:D, U3 -+ B:D) |> 
  initialize_graph()

dag_list_independences(duarg)

duarg2 <- dag_transform_merge_latents(duarg)

drels <- dag_get_linear_relations(duarg2)
dhreps <- cf_relations_to_hrep(drels)

nontriv <- prob_simplex_extremes(drels, dhreps$Hrep)
lapply(nontriv, sum)

doprobs1 <- glue::glue_data(drels$problevels[[1]], paste0("P(", paste0(drels$poterms[[1]]$out, " = {", drels$poterms[[1]]$out, "}", collapse = ", "), "| do(", 
       paste0(drels$poterms[[1]]$do, " = {", drels$poterms[[1]]$do, "}", collapse = ", "), "))"))
hrep_to_text(dhreps$Hrep[[1]], doprobs1)[nontriv[[1]]]
#hrep_to_text(dhreps$Hrep[[2]], drels$probform[[2]])[nontriv[[2]]]
```



## Front door model

```{r}
fd <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(A -+ M -+ Y, U1 -+ A:Y))
dag_list_independences(fd)

fdrels <- dag_get_linear_relations(fd)
fdreps <- cf_relations_to_hrep(fdrels)

hrep_to_text(fdreps$Hrep[[1]], prob = fdrels$probform[[1]])[prob_simplex_extremes(fdrels, fdreps$Hrep)[[1]]]

## all trivial
hrep_to_text(fdreps$Hrep[[2]], prob = fdrels$probform[[2]])

unfd <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(A +- M -+ Y, U1 -+ A:Y))
res <- matrix(NA, nrow = 1000, ncol = nrow(fdreps$Hrep[[1]]))

for(i in 1:nrow(res)) {

  probs <- dag_sample_distribution(unfd, parmsamp = \(k) rnorm(k, sd = 5))
  probs1 <- merge(probs$Y, probs$A, by = "M", all = TRUE)
  probs2 <- merge(probs1, probs$M, by = "M", all = TRUE)
  
  probs2$probf <- with(probs2, probs.x * probs.y * probs)
  probs2 <- probs2[with(probs2, order(M, Y, A)),]


  res[i,] <- hrep_test(fdreps$Hrep[[1]], probs2$probf, which = TRUE)[, 1]
             
}

hrep_to_text(fdreps$Hrep[[1]], fdrels$probform[[1]])[colMeans(res) < 1]
```




## More difficult example


```{r}
d1 <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(V1 -+ V2, V2 -+ V3, V3 -+ V4, U1 -+ V1:V3, U2 -+ V2:V4))
plot(d1)
```

This has no conditional independences: 
```{r}
dag_list_independences(d1)
```

It does however have a nontrivial inequality constraint that we can find. 

```{r}
d1rels <- dag_get_linear_relations(d1)
hrepd1 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(d1rels)
#hrep_to_text(hrepd1$Hrep[[2]], d1rels$probform[[2]])
```

Let's sample some probability distributions without any restrictions as see if anything is violated. 

```{r}
probs <- dag_sample_distribution(d1, parmsamp = \(k) rnorm(k, sd = 5))

probs1 <- merge(probs$V3, probs$V1, by = NULL)
probs1$prob <- with(probs1, probs.x * probs.y)
probs1 <- probs1[with(probs1, order(V2, V3, V1)),]

hrep_test(hrepd1$Hrep[[1]], probs1$prob)


probs2 <- merge(probs$V4, probs$V2, by = NULL)
probs2$prob <- with(probs2, probs.x * probs.y)
probs2 <- probs2[with(probs2, order(V3, V1, V4, V2)),]

hrep_test(hrepd1$Hrep[[2]], probs2$prob)
```

Great, nothing is violated if we sample a distribution from the DAG, but let's see what happens when sampling from an unconstrained model: 

```{r}
dun <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(V1 -+ V2:V4:V3, V2 -+ V3:V4, V3 -+ V4, U1 -+ V1:V2:V3:V4))
plot(dun)


res <- matrix(NA, nrow = 1000, ncol = sum(sapply(hrepd1$Hrep, nrow)))
for(i in 1:nrow(res)) {

  probs <- dag_sample_distribution(dun, parmsamp = \(k) rnorm(k, sd = 5))
  probs1 <- merge(probs$V3, probs$V1, by = "V1")
  probs1$prob <- with(probs1, probs.x * probs.y)
  probs1 <- probs1[with(probs1, order(V2, V3, V1)),]

  probs2 <- merge(probs$V4, probs$V2, by = c("V1", "V2"))
  probs2$prob <- with(probs2, probs.x * probs.y)
  probs2 <- probs2[with(probs2, order(V3, V1, V4, V2)),]

  res[i,] <- c(hrep_test(hrepd1$Hrep[[1]], probs1$prob, which = TRUE), 
               hrep_test(hrepd1$Hrep[[2]], probs2$prob, which = TRUE))
}

sapply(hrepd1$Hrep, nrow)
which(colMeans(res) < 1)
```

So none of the first set of constraints on probabilities of the form `r `d1rels$probform[[1]][[1]]` are nontrivial, but the following ones are: 

```{r}
cat(hrep_to_text(hrepd1$Hrep[[2]], d1rels$probform[[2]])[which(colMeans(res)[-c(1:11)] < 1)], sep = "\n")
```

Some of these are inequality constraints, which were previously unknown. 



## Test graph

```{r}
d2 <- initialize_graph(graph_from_literal(V0 -+ V1:V4, V1 -+ V2 -+ V3 -+ V4, Ur -+ V2:V4))
plot(d2)
```

This has some conditional independences: 
```{r}
dag_list_independences(d2)
```

It does however have a nontrivial inequality constraint that we can find. 

```{r}
d2rels <- dag_get_linear_relations(d2)
hrepd2 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(d2rels$probform[2], d2rels$relation[2])
hrep_to_text(hrepd2$Hrep[[2]], d2rels$probform[[2]])

hrepd2 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(d2rels$probform, d2rels$relation)

```


## Bi/Tripartite Bell scenario

```{r}
bell2 <- graph_from_literal(X -+ A, Y -+ B, Ur -+ A:B) |> initialize_graph()
#V(bell2)[c("A", "B")]$nvals <- 3
b2rels <- dag_get_linear_relations(bell2)
hrepb2 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(b2rels$probform, b2rels$relation)
hrep_to_text(hrepb2$Hrep[[1]], b2rels$probform)[prob_simplex_extremes(b2rels, hrepb2$Hrep)[[1]]]

```


```{r}
bell3 <- graph_from_literal(X -+ A, Y -+ B, Z -+ C, Ur -+ A:B:C) |> initialize_graph()
dag_list_independences(bell3)
b3rels <- dag_get_linear_relations(bell3)
hrepb3 <- cf_relations_to_hrep(b3rels$probform, b3rels$relation)
hrep <- hrepb3$Hrep[[1]]

ctabin <- split(b3rels$problevels[[1]], b3rels$problevels[[1]][, b3rels$poterms[[1]]$do])
constgrps <- lapply(ctabin, \(cin) {
        # res <- c(glue::glue_data(cin,
        #                   paste(c("p", paste0("{", b3rels$poterms[[i]]$out, "}"),
        #                         "d", paste0("{", b3rels$poterms[[i]]$do, "}")),
        #                         collapse = "")))
        res <- do.call(paste, c(as.list(cin), sep = "."))
        res
})

fast_htest <- function(l, b, a, probform, tol = 1e-10, which = FALSE) {

  axb <- a %*% probform - b

  chk <- axb <= tol & abs(l * axb) <= tol
  if(which) {
    chk
  } else {
    all(chk)
  }

}


rawprobs <- unlist(b3rels$probform[[1]])


  l <- hrep[ , 1]
  b <- hrep[ , 2]
  a <- -hrep[ , - c(1, 2)]

set1<- sapply(constgrps,"[", 1)
combos <- combinations(rep(length(constgrps[[1]]), length(constgrps))) + 1
    
nontrivial <- rep(FALSE, nrow(hrep))
for(j in 1:nrow(combos)) {
  theseprobs <- rep(0, length(rawprobs))
  names(theseprobs) <- names(rawprobs)
  for(k in 1:ncol(combos)) {
      theseprobs[constgrps[[k]][combos[j, k]]] <- 1
  }

  htest <- !fast_htest(l, b, a, theseprobs, tol = 1e-8, which = TRUE)[,1]
  if(any(htest)) {
        nontrivial[which(htest)] <- TRUE
        l <- l[-which(htest)]
        b <- b[-which(htest)]
        a <- a[-which(htest),]
      }
      
      #allprobs[j, ] <- theseprobs

}
    
    


b3tcons <-hrep_to_text(hrepb3$Hrep[[1]], b3rels$probform[[1]])

doprobs <- glue::glue_data(b3rels$problevels[[1]],
  paste0("P(", paste(paste0(b3rels$poterms[[1]]$out, " = {", b3rels$poterms[[1]]$out, "}"), collapse = ", "), " | do(", 
  paste(paste0(b3rels$poterms[[1]]$do, " = {", b3rels$poterms[[1]]$do, "}"), collapse = ", "), "))"))

b3docon <- hrep_to_text(hrepb3$Hrep[[1]], doprobs)

table(hrepb3$Hrep[[1]][,1]== 1)
b3docon[hrepb3$Hrep[[1]][,1] == 0 & nontrivial][1:4]

```
